_note: The training league: an INDEPENDENTLY-trained population on the same roster and the same run mechanics as small_league.json, diverging purely from a different nondeterministic training trajectory. That is the whole design -- a shared, population-wide blind spot is something an independently-evolved population exposes and a deck's own history never can. Everything below is what genuinely differs from small_league.json (league_name, and training_league_name pointing BACK at it so validation's primary_vs_training_round_robin check reports against the main league from this population's first session); mechanics, roster, and total_games are inherited via "extends" -- they used to be retyped here and had silently drifted once already (games_per_iteration and pfsp_power were absent, so this trained at 6 games/iteration against the main league's 24), which is exactly the kind of difference that makes a training-league comparison measure the config instead of the training; extends makes that drift structurally impossible now instead of relying on a test to catch it. The confound that disabled the ORIGINAL twin population is now structurally impossible for an unrelated reason too: it was trained against a frozen shared stack that was later deleted, and its weights were then loaded onto the calling population's unrelated embedding space -- silently invalid, not a crash. Per-deck encoders (2026-08-17) put the encoder inside each checkpoint, so a population can only ever be played through the perception it was trained with, and the stack_id.txt guard that policed this is gone.
_history_note: Renamed 2026-08-23 from run_gauntlet_twin.json, and folded in what used to be a separate one-time creation config (run_gauntlet_pod.json / training_league_4deck_init.json, extends-free, total_games hardcoded to 10000) -- two files to drive one population was needless: this file's own "extends" already inherits everything the init config duplicated. The checkpoint (checkpoints/4_deck_subleague_gauntlet/progress.json) currently sits at 5,016 games/deck, short of even that old 10,000 target -- training stopped there regardless of which config was nominally driving it.
